title: NoBrow Tongue 솔로 #018 · 혀 구멍 1개 + 링·굵은 체인 추 · 혀 색 선홍 · 뱀 눈 짙은 푸른 · 중국 30대 · 도도한 · 인어 세이렌 · 유형 고유 메이크업 · P100
prompt:
Professional fashion photograph, close-up beauty portrait. ONE woman, facing the camera straight on in a perfectly frontal portrait, her head level, both ears clearly visible on either side of her face, framed tightly from the very top of her head down to the line of her shoulders, the frame cutting off just below them, so the weights fully hang in view. Her face is large and sharp. Mid 30s.

Subject: A real photograph of a strikingly beautiful, seductive adult woman, mid 20s, a mermaid siren brought to life: dewy skin with real visible pores as if just risen from the sea, with iridescent pearlescent teal-and-opal scale-shaped highlights shimmering on her cheekbones, temples and along her jaw, long wet-look wavy hair in pearl-white falling past her shoulders. Her eyes are large, almond, slightly upturned, real snake eyes: large glossy deep electric blue irises with a razor-thin vertical slit pupil, jet black, running the full height of each eye, both eyes the same, the colour solidly saturated across the whole iris with a darker ring around its edge, a wet glassy shine on the surface of each eye, set in her ordinary human eyelids and sitting clear of the eyelid edges, with bright catchlights, with pearlescent aqua eyeshadow, a soft glittering wing and long, dark lashes. Her lips are full, glossy, wet-looking coral-pink, parted just slightly. High, glowing cheekbones, a small straight nose and a delicate chin. A dreamy, magnetic, alluring gaze straight into the camera. Every feature is exaggerated but beautiful, balanced and refined, in harmony with the rest of her face, never distorted, never grotesque. Her whole face, ears and neck are real living flesh with real pores and fine skin grain and a soft sheen of natural oils, individual hair strands catching the light — a photograph of a real woman's face, not an illustration, not a render. Her brows are bare like the Mona Lisa's: the whole brow bone is smooth, hairless skin in the same tone as her forehead, with only the soft natural curve of the brow ridge showing, her forehead high, smooth and serene. Her mouth is wide open and her tongue is stretched out far, long, broad and flat, glossy bright scarlet red, hanging low past her lower lip with a smooth rounded tip, and it has a hole through its centre: a big clean round hole about the size of a coin at the middle of the tongue, about halfway along its length, straight through the full thickness of the tongue, its edge lined with a thin polished metal eyelet ring, a thick polished metal ring passes through the hole, and from that ring a heavy chain with thick links hangs straight down over her lower lip and chin with dull pewter-grey tin a chunky hexagonal nut-shaped weight with a round hole through the centre at its end, a massive, dense lump of rough, matte, unpolished metal at least as big as her whole fist, hanging freely in the air in front of her chin and neck, the weight ending no lower than the level of her collarbones and never resting on her chest or body, the whole tongue clearly visible and in sharp focus (this overrides the lips pressed or closed in her expression).

Piercings: A face fully covered with real piercings, about sixty-six in total (not counting the hanging weights), spread over every area so that no area is empty: a single large septum ring of different sizes and shapes through the thin soft wall between the nostrils, in a short stack that ends above the upper lip; two small rings wrapping snugly around each nostril wing; five small ring or studs on the chin; on each ear, one large healed opening in the earlobe holding a very thick, heavy black cast-iron ring as thick as a finger, a plain solid ring with no open tunnel, and above it sit fourteen pieces above the lobe: seven classic round O-rings and studs along the helix rim, four studs and small bars across the upper cartilage and three in the conch and tragus; ten small studs across the lower half of the forehead just above the brows in even rows, leaving the upper forehead free; eight small studs along each cheekbone, well clear of the eyes. The left and right sides are balanced. The piercings are packed so densely that the rows touch and overlap, leaving only hairline gaps of bare skin between them, until the face reads as a single armour of metal; the eyes and eyelids stay clear. Henna: fine metallic gold henna mehndi line patterns of vines and dots are painted across the upper forehead near the hairline only, above the forehead studs, well clear of the eyes and brows. Stickers: five tiny glow-in-the-dark heart and star stickers are scattered flat on the skin of the lower cheeks and the jawline below the cheekbone studs, clear of the piercings, the eyes and the lips. All the ear weights hang from the bottoms of this iron ring, and they are not counted in the piercing total: on each ear there are exactly ten separate massive weights, each of a different shape, all of them dark brown bronze with a rough cast, uneven surface and green-black patina, each hanging on its own thick heavy chain of the same metal: on the left ear a pyramid-shaped lump on a shortest chain, a ship's anchor on a shortest chain, a teardrop-shaped sinker on a short chain, a chunky hexagonal nut-shaped weight with a round hole through the centre on a short chain, a square-sided cowbell on a medium chain, a hammer head on a long chain, a miniature anvil on a long chain, a cube-shaped block on a longer chain, a barrel-shaped weight on a longer chain, a bell-shaped weight like a small temple bell with a flared rim on a longest chain; on the right ear a miniature anvil on a shortest chain, a chunky hexagonal nut-shaped weight with a round hole through the centre on a shortest chain, a bell-shaped weight like a small temple bell with a flared rim on a short chain, a ship's anchor on a short chain, a round bell on a medium chain, a barrel-shaped weight on a long chain, a cube-shaped block on a long chain, a pyramid-shaped lump on a longer chain, a hammer head on a longer chain, a square-sided cowbell on a longest chain. On each ear the single iron ring carries all the weights, hanging in a staggered cluster on chains of different lengths and staggered at different heights so every weight is fully visible and none hides another. Every single weight is a massive, dense, solid lump of metal at least as big as her whole fist and clearly larger than her earlobe, rough and matte and unpolished with no shine and no delicate or thin parts; its size does NOT shrink just because there are many of them: the last weight is exactly as big, as thick and as heavy-looking as the first. Each weight alone looks like it weighs several kilograms, each chain is pulled bar-straight and taut, and at a glance every single one looks crushingly, unmistakably heavy, the chains hanging freely in the air, clear of her neck and shoulders, with even the longest chain and its weight ending no lower than the level of her collarbones, never below them and never resting on her chest or body. Because all the load is carried by one opening, the weight gently pulls each earlobe down a little into a slightly elongated, soft, healthy loop of skin, only a small natural droop that is just enough to show how heavy the weights are; the lobe never stretches long, never tears or collapses and never hangs down to her neck or shoulder, her head stays upright, and the skin stays smooth and intact, fully healed, with no tearing, no wound, no blood and no redness. The face and ear jewelry is real blackened steel set with small clear diamonds, one-colour, restrained, while the hanging weights are always rough, matte, unpolished bronze, sitting in real, calm, healthy skin — no redness, no swelling, no irritation — with a small natural warm shadow under each piece. Every piece stays at least a finger's width from the eyeballs, and no chain or bar crosses the eyes. In addition to all of the above, her tongue carries a few piercings in the same metal and gems: three straight barbells threaded sideways through the base of the tongue, evenly spaced, each bar hidden inside the tissue with only its two round end balls showing at the outer edges of the tongue, and a barbell threaded sideways through the tongue just behind the tip, its bar hidden inside the tissue with only the two round balls showing at the edges, the pieces spread along the tongue so that every one reads individually with bare tissue between them and the hole. From the tip of the tongue a thin, glistening strand of saliva falls straight down, catching the light.

Piercing depth: every bar and surface bar is embedded in the skin — its middle runs beneath the skin so only its two end studs show on the surface, the skin between them faintly raised over the hidden bar, with a small warm shadow at each end and nothing lying on top of the skin like a sticker. Every ring passes through a small healed opening in the skin, the skin visible through the loop, and every stud sits through the skin with its back hidden. Where a bar, ring or stud goes through the ear, the lip, the nostril or the brow, it passes through the real tissue with the skin wrapping snugly around it. Tongue piercing depth: every barbell on the tongue runs beneath the surface, its bar hidden inside the flesh so that only its two round end balls show on the surface, the tissue faintly raised over the hidden bar with a small warm shadow at each ball, and every eyelet lines a hole through the real wet healthy tongue tissue, calm and healthy with no redness, no swelling and no irritation. The tongue stays stretched out at its full length, broad and flat, despite the weights.

Hair: her hair is swept back behind both ears, leaving both ears, her jawline and her neck fully visible so every hanging piece is in clear view.

Lighting: MANDATORY pure pitch black void background only, absolutely NO studio backdrop NO texture NO grey NO gradient. A soft frontal light on her face and ears, so the glints on every piece of metal read clearly against her skin; a thin cool rim light along the hair and shoulders. 2:3 vertical 8K portrait.
